items: Rank = number of non-zero rows in row-echelon form. rank(AB) ≤ min(rank A, rank B).
Ax = b with n unknowns: rank[A|b] ≠ rank A → no solution; rank[A|b] = rank A = n → unique; = rank A = r < n → infinitely many, with n − r free variables.
Homogeneous Ax = 0 is always consistent; a square A has a non-trivial solution only if det A = 0.
Sum of eigenvalues = trace A; product = det A. Triangular or diagonal matrix: eigenvalues are the diagonal entries.
If λ is an eigenvalue of A: Aᵏ → λᵏ, A⁻¹ → 1/λ, A + kI → λ + k, kA → kλ. Eigenvectors stay the same.
Real symmetric → real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors. Skew-symmetric → 0 or purely imaginary. Orthogonal → |λ| = 1.
Cayley–Hamilton: A satisfies its own characteristic equation. Use it to get A⁻¹ or high powers of A.
A matrix with all rows proportional has rank 1, so n − 1 eigenvalues are 0 and the last equals the trace.
Eigenvectors of distinct eigenvalues are linearly independent; A is diagonalizable only with n independent eigenvectors.

Matrix algebra and rank: Types of matrices: symmetric, skew-symmetric, orthogonal, Hermitian, unitary
Inverse by adjoint and by row operations
Elementary row operations and echelon form
Rank by echelon form and by minors

Eigenvalues of symmetric, orthogonal and triangular matrices
Cayley-Hamilton theorem and special matr: Cayley–Hamilton statement and check on a 2×2 matrix
Quadratic forms and definiteness from eigenvalues
Rank-1 matrices (u vᵀ) and their eigenvalues

items: Standard limits: sin x / x → 1, (1 + 1/x)ˣ → e, (aˣ − 1)/x → ln a. Use L'Hôpital only for 0/0 or ∞/∞.
Rolle: f(a) = f(b) ⇒ f′(c) = 0 for some c in (a, b). LMVT: f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a).
Two-variable extrema at fx = fy = 0: r = fxx, s = fxy, t = fyy. rt − s² > 0 and r < 0 → max; r > 0 → min; rt − s² < 0 → saddle.
∫₀ᵃ f(x) dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a − x) dx. Odd function over symmetric limits → 0. Even → 2∫₀ᵃ.
Wallis: ∫₀^{π/2} sinⁿx dx = (n−1)/n · (n−3)/(n−2) … × (π/2 if n even, 1 if n odd).
Euler: f homogeneous of degree n ⇒ x fx + y fy = n f.
Taylor: eˣ = 1 + x + x²/2! + …, sin x = x − x³/3! + …, ln(1 + x) = x − x²/2 + x³/3 − …
|x| is continuous but not differentiable at 0. Check left and right derivatives separately.
Global max/min on a closed interval: also check the endpoints, not only stationary points.

Limits, continuity, differentiability: Continuity at a point and types of discontinuity
Special functions: |x|, x sin(1/x), floor function
Mean value theorems: Checking whether a theorem applies on an interval
Maxima and minima: Global extrema on a closed interval
Definite integrals and applications: Properties of definite integrals (a − x, symmetry, periodicity)
Double integrals and change of order
Taylor series: Standard expansions: eˣ, sin x, cos x, ln(1 + x), (1 + x)ⁿ

items: Linear first order y′ + P y = Q: integrating factor IF = e^{∫P dx}; then y·IF = ∫Q·IF dx + c.
M dx + N dy = 0 is exact when ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x.
Constant coefficients, roots of auxiliary equation: real distinct → c₁e^{m₁x} + c₂e^{m₂x}; repeated → (c₁ + c₂x)e^{mx}; α ± jβ → e^{αx}(c₁cos βx + c₂sin βx).
Particular integral for e^{ax}: e^{ax}/f(a). If f(a) = 0, multiply by x and use f′(a).
Cauchy–Euler x²y″ + a x y′ + b y = 0: try y = xᵐ, giving m(m − 1) + a m + b = 0.
Wronskian ≠ 0 ⇒ solutions are linearly independent.
Order = highest derivative; degree = power of that derivative after removing radicals and fractions.
For an IVP, apply initial conditions to the complete solution (CF + PI), not to the CF alone.

Higher order linear ODEs: Particular integrals for e^{ax}, sin/cos, xⁿ, e^{ax}V
Initial and boundary value problems: Applying initial conditions to the complete solution
Solving ODEs with the Laplace transform
Physical applications: RLC circuits, mass–spring systems

items: Analytic ⇔ Cauchy–Riemann: uₓ = v_y and u_y = −vₓ (with continuous partials). Then u and v are harmonic.
Cauchy theorem: ∮ f(z) dz = 0 if f is analytic inside and on C.
Cauchy integral formula: ∮ f(z)/(z − a) dz = 2πj f(a); ∮ f(z)/(z − a)^{n+1} dz = 2πj f⁽ⁿ⁾(a)/n!.
Residue at a simple pole: lim (z − a) f(z), or p(a)/q′(a) for f = p/q. Pole of order m: (1/(m−1)!) d^{m−1}/dz^{m−1} [(z − a)ᵐ f(z)] at z = a.
Residue theorem: ∮ f dz = 2πj × (sum of residues of poles inside C).
In a Laurent series about a, the residue is the coefficient of 1/(z − a).
Always check which poles lie inside the contour (|z| = r or |z − z₀| = r) before adding residues.
The region of validity decides which Laurent expansion to use (|z| < 1 vs |z| > 1).

Analytic functions and Cauchy-Riemann eq: Complex numbers, polar form, De Moivre, roots
Limits and continuity of complex functions
Cauchy integral theorem and formula: Line integrals in the complex plane
Cauchy's integral formula and formula for derivatives
Taylor and Laurent series: Laurent series in different annular regions
Zeros and classification of singularities (removable, pole, essential)
Residue theorem: Residue at a simple pole and at a pole of order m
Real integrals over 0 to 2π using z = e^{jθ}

items: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Independent: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). Bayes: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
Binomial: mean np, variance npq. Poisson: mean = variance = λ.
Uniform(a, b): mean (a + b)/2, variance (b − a)²/12. Exponential(λ): mean 1/λ, variance 1/λ², memoryless.
Normal: about 68%, 95%, 99.7% within 1σ, 2σ, 3σ.
Var(aX + b) = a² Var X. Var(X + Y) = Var X + Var Y + 2 Cov(X, Y).
Correlation ρ = Cov(X, Y)/(σx σy), with |ρ| ≤ 1. Independent ⇒ uncorrelated (not the reverse).
For X, Y uniform on (0, 1) and independent: E[max] = 2/3, E[min] = 1/3.
A PDF must integrate to 1: use this to find an unknown constant first.

Probability and Bayes theorem: Sample space, axioms and addition rule
Random variables and standard distributi: Discrete and continuous random variables: PMF, PDF, CDF

items: Newton–Raphson: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ); quadratic convergence. Bisection: linear, error halves each step.
Trapezoidal: (h/2)[y₀ + 2(y₁ + … + yₙ₋₁) + yₙ], error O(h²). Simpson 1/3 (n even): (h/3)[y₀ + 4(odd) + 2(even) + yₙ], exact for cubics.
Euler's method: y₁ = y₀ + h f(x₀, y₀).
∇ × (∇f) = 0 and ∇ · (∇ × A) = 0 always.
Divergence theorem: ∯ A · dS = ∭ ∇ · A dV. Stokes: ∮ A · dl = ∬ (∇ × A) · dS.
Directional derivative = ∇f · â; it is largest along ∇f with value |∇f|.
Simpson's 1/3 needs an even number of intervals; 3/8 rule needs a multiple of 3.
A conservative field has zero curl and a path-independent line integral.

Numerical integration: Newton forward and backward interpolation basics
Green, Stokes and Gauss theorems: Choosing the easier side of a theorem in problems

items: Thevenin: Vth = open-circuit voltage; Rth = Voc/Isc. With dependent sources, keep them on and apply a test source.
Max power: R_L = R_th (DC), P_max = Vth²/(4Rth). AC: Z_L = Z_th*; if only a resistor can vary, R_L = |Z_th|.
Superposition works for V and I, not power. Dependent sources are never switched off.
First-order response: x(t) = x(∞) + [x(0⁺) − x(∞)] e^{−t/τ}, τ = RC or L/R with the Thevenin R seen by C or L.
Capacitor voltage and inductor current cannot jump. At DC steady state: C is open, L is short.
Series RLC: ω₀ = 1/√(LC), α = R/2L, ζ = α/ω₀; Q = ω₀L/R; BW = R/L = ω₀/Q. Parallel RLC: Q = R√(C/L), BW = 1/RC.
Graph: tree has n − 1 branches; independent loops (links) = b − n + 1.
Two-port: reciprocal → z₁₂ = z₂₁, y₁₂ = y₂₁, h₁₂ = −h₂₁, AD − BC = 1. Symmetric → z₁₁ = z₂₂, A = D.
Complex power S = V I* = P + jQ; power factor = cos φ.
At t = 0⁺ an uncharged capacitor acts as a short and an unfluxed inductor as an open.
Use RMS values in power formulas; phasors from peak values need a factor of 1/2.

topics: Causality and stability of LTI systems

items: LTI output y = x * h. Causal ⇔ h(t) = 0 for t < 0. BIBO stable ⇔ ∫|h(t)| dt < ∞.
Discrete convolution of lengths N₁ and N₂ has length N₁ + N₂ − 1. Area of x * h = (area of x)(area of h).
Pairs: e^{−at}u(t) ↔ 1/(a + jω); rect(t/T) ↔ T sinc(fT); δ(t) ↔ 1; x(t − t₀) ↔ e^{−jωt₀}X(ω); x(at) ↔ X(ω/a)/|a|.
Parseval: ∫|x(t)|² dt = (1/2π)∫|X(ω)|² dω.
Laplace ROC: right-sided → right of the rightmost pole. Stable ⇔ ROC contains the jω axis.
Z-transform: aⁿu[n] ↔ 1/(1 − a z⁻¹), |z| > |a|. Causal and stable ⇔ all poles inside the unit circle.
Sampling: fs ≥ 2 f_max. An undersampled tone at f appears at |f − k fs|.
N-point DFT multiplication = circular convolution. Radix-2 FFT: (N/2) log₂N complex multiplications.
Group delay τg = −dθ/dω; phase delay τp = −θ(ω)/ω.
Final value theorem applies only when all poles of sX(s) are in the left half plane.
Fourier series of a signal with half-wave symmetry has only odd harmonics.

Signal classification and operations: Even/odd and periodic signals, fundamental period
Unit step, impulse, ramp and their relations
System properties: Testing properties on given system equations

items: Mass action law: n·p = nᵢ². kT/q ≈ 25.9 mV at 300 K. Silicon nᵢ ≈ 1.5 × 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ (some papers use 10¹⁰).
Conductivity σ = q(n μn + p μp). Einstein relation D/μ = kT/q. Diffusion length L = √(Dτ).
Built-in potential Vbi = (kT/q) ln(NA ND / nᵢ²).
Depletion width W = √[(2ε(Vbi + VR)/q)(1/NA + 1/ND)]; it extends mostly into the lightly doped side (xn/xp = NA/ND).
Junction capacitance Cj = εA/W ∝ (Vbi + VR)^{−1/2} for an abrupt junction, ^{−1/3} for linearly graded.
Diode: I = Is(e^{V/ηVT} − 1). Is roughly doubles every 10 °C.
MOSFET saturation: ID = (μnCox/2)(W/L)(VGS − VT)²(1 + λVDS); gm = 2ID/(VGS − VT). Linear: ID = μnCox(W/L)[(VGS − VT)VDS − VDS²/2].
Body effect: VT = VT0 + γ[√(2φF + VSB) − √(2φF)].
MOS capacitor: accumulation → depletion → inversion; threshold when surface potential = 2φF.
Zener breakdown (< ~5 V) has a negative temperature coefficient; avalanche (> ~6 V) positive.
LEDs need direct-bandgap material (GaAs); silicon is indirect. Photodiodes work in reverse bias.

Energy bands and crystal structure: Energy bands in metals, semiconductors and insulators

items: BJT: IC = βIB, IE = (β + 1)IB, α = β/(β + 1); gm = IC/VT; rπ = β/gm; ro = VA/IC.
CE gain ≈ −gm(RC ∥ RL); with unbypassed RE ≈ −RC/RE. CC: gain ≈ 1, high Rin, low Rout. CB: Rin ≈ 1/gm, current gain ≈ 1.
CS gain −gm(RD ∥ ro); CD ≈ gmR/(1 + gmR); CG input resistance ≈ 1/gm.
Miller effect: Cin = C(1 − Av). It sets the upper cutoff of CE/CS stages.
Differential pair: Ad = gmRC (differential output); CMRR = |Ad/Ac|, improved by a large tail resistance.
Negative feedback: Af = A/(1 + Aβ). Series mixing raises Rin; shunt lowers it. Voltage sampling lowers Rout; current sampling raises it.
Op-amp: inverting −Rf/R1; non-inverting 1 + Rf/R1. Full-power bandwidth f = SR/(2πVm). Gain × bandwidth is constant.
Barkhausen: loop gain = 1, phase 0°. RC phase shift: f = 1/(2πRC√6), gain ≥ 29. Wien bridge: f = 1/(2πRC), gain ≥ 3.
Rectifiers: half-wave Vdc = Vm/π, ripple factor 1.21; full-wave Vdc = 2Vm/π, ripple 0.482. PIV: half-wave Vm, centre-tap 2Vm, bridge Vm.
Power amps: class A max 25% (resistive load), 50% (transformer); class B 78.5%; class AB removes crossover distortion.
555 astable: f = 1.44/((RA + 2RB)C).
In small-signal analysis, DC supplies become ground and coupling/bypass capacitors become shorts.
Check the transistor region first (active, saturation, cutoff) before using any gain formula.

Diode circuits: clippers, clampers, rect: Diode models: ideal, constant drop, small-signal

Input resistance, output resistance and gain of each

items: n-bit 2's complement range: −2ⁿ⁻¹ to 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1. Overflow when carry into MSB ≠ carry out of MSB.
Consensus theorem: AB + A′C + BC = AB + A′C. NAND and NOR are universal gates.
K-map groups are 1, 2, 4, 8 adjacent cells, including wrap-around. Use don't-cares only to enlarge groups.
A 2ⁿ:1 MUX can implement any function of n + 1 variables. Decoder + OR gate implements any SOP.
Flip-flops: JK Q⁺ = JQ′ + K′Q; T Q⁺ = T ⊕ Q; D Q⁺ = D.
Ripple counter delay = n·tpd; synchronous = one tpd. Mod-N needs ⌈log₂N⌉ flip-flops. Ring counter: mod-n; Johnson: mod-2n.
Noise margins: NMH = VOH − VIH, NML = VIL − VOL. CMOS has near-zero static power.
DAC resolution = Vref/2ⁿ. Flash ADC needs 2ⁿ − 1 comparators (fastest); successive approximation takes n clock cycles; dual slope is slow but accurate.
A 2ⁿ × m memory has n address lines and m data lines.
Race-around occurs in level-triggered JK when J = K = 1 and the clock pulse is longer than the propagation delay.
XOR of n inputs is 1 when an odd number of inputs are 1.

topics: Signal flow graphs and Mason gain formula
Time response of first and second order systems

items: Closed loop T = G/(1 + GH). Sensitivity of T to G = 1/(1 + GH). Mason: T = Σ PkΔk / Δ.
Second order: Mp = e^{−ζπ/√(1−ζ²)}; tp = π/ωd; ts ≈ 4/(ζωn) (2% band); ωd = ωn√(1 − ζ²).
Steady-state error: type 0 step → 1/(1 + Kp); type 1 ramp → 1/Kv; type 2 parabola → 1/Ka.
Routh: sign changes in the first column = number of RHP poles. Row of zeros → use the auxiliary polynomial (symmetric roots).

Root locus: starts at open-loop poles, ends at zeros or infinity. Asymptote angles (2q + 1)180°/(P − Z); centroid (Σ poles − Σ zeros)/(P − Z). Real-axis part lies left of an odd count of poles + zeros.
Bode: each pole −20 dB/dec and −90°; each zero +20 dB/dec and +90°. GM = −20 log|G(jωpc)|; PM = 180° + ∠G(jωgc).
Nyquist: Z = P + N (N = clockwise encirclements of −1). Closed loop stable when Z = 0.
Lead improves transient response and PM; lag improves steady-state error.
State space: T(s) = C(sI − A)⁻¹B + D. Eigenvalues of A are the poles. φ(t) = L⁻¹[(sI − A)⁻¹].
Controllable ⇔ rank[B AB … Aⁿ⁻¹B] = n. Observable ⇔ rank[C; CA; …; CAⁿ⁻¹] = n.
System type counts poles of G(s)H(s) at the origin, not closed-loop poles.
Pole-zero cancellation can hide an uncontrollable or unobservable mode.

items: AM: Pt = Pc(1 + μ²/2); efficiency μ²/(2 + μ²), max 33.3% at μ = 1. BW: AM and DSB-SC 2fm, SSB fm.
FM: β = Δf/fm. Carson bandwidth = 2(Δf + fm). Total power is constant.
Superheterodyne: image frequency = fs + 2 f_IF (when LO is above the signal).
Friis noise: F = F₁ + (F₂ − 1)/G₁ + (F₃ − 1)/(G₁G₂) + … Thermal noise power = kTB.
PCM: SQNR ≈ 6.02n + 1.76 dB for a full-scale sinusoid; bit rate = n·fs. Each extra bit adds 6 dB.
Nyquist ISI-free minimum BW = Rb/2; raised cosine BW = (Rb/2)(1 + α).
Matched filter h(t) = s(T − t); peak output SNR = 2E/N₀.
BER: BPSK Pe = Q(√(2Eb/N₀)); coherent BFSK Q(√(Eb/N₀)); QPSK has BPSK's bit error rate in half the bandwidth.
WSS: constant mean, R(τ) depends only on τ. PSD = Fourier transform of R(τ). Output PSD = |H(f)|² × input PSD.
Entropy H = −Σ p log₂p (max log₂M for equiprobable). Shannon C = B log₂(1 + S/N).
Block code with minimum distance d: detects d − 1 errors, corrects ⌊(d − 1)/2⌋.
White noise of two-sided PSD N₀/2 through an ideal LPF of bandwidth B gives noise power N₀B.
AM with μ > 1 over-modulates: the envelope detector distorts.

topics: Standing waves, VSWR and impedance matching

items: Maxwell: ∇·D = ρv, ∇·B = 0, ∇×E = −∂B/∂t, ∇×H = J + ∂D/∂t.
Boundaries: tangential E continuous; normal D jumps by ρs; normal B continuous; tangential H jumps by Js.
Lossless medium: v = 1/√(με), η = √(μ/ε); free space η₀ = 120π ≈ 377 Ω.
Skin depth δ = 1/√(πfμσ). Good conductor when σ/(ωε) ≫ 1.
Normal incidence: Γ = (η₂ − η₁)/(η₂ + η₁), τ = 1 + Γ. Brewster angle tan θB = √(ε₂/ε₁) (parallel polarization).
Average Poynting vector of a plane wave: E₀²/(2η).
Lines: Z₀ = √(L/C); Γ_L = (Z_L − Z₀)/(Z_L + Z₀); VSWR = (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|); Zin = Z₀(Z_L + jZ₀ tan βl)/(Z₀ + jZ_L tan βl).
Quarter-wave line: Zin = Z₀²/Z_L. Half-wave line repeats Z_L.
Rectangular guide: TE₁₀ cutoff fc = c/(2a); λg = λ/√(1 − (fc/f)²). No TEM mode in a hollow guide; lowest TM is TM₁₁.
Half-wave dipole: Rrad ≈ 73 Ω, directivity 1.64. Friis: Pr = Pt Gt Gr (λ/4πR)². Effective aperture Ae = Gλ²/4π.
A short-circuited line shorter than λ/4 looks inductive; open-circuited looks capacitive.
Below cutoff a waveguide mode is evanescent: no power flows.

topics: PMMC, moving iron and electrodynamometer instruments

items: Limiting error: products and quotients add relative errors; sums and differences add absolute errors.
PMMC: DC only, linear scale. Moving iron: AC and DC, square-law scale. Electrodynamometer: AC/DC, used in wattmeters.
Ammeter shunt Rsh = Rm/(m − 1). Voltmeter multiplier Rse = Rm(m − 1).
Bridges: Wheatstone (medium R), Kelvin double (low R), Maxwell (medium-Q inductors), Hay (high-Q inductors), Schering (capacitance and loss), Wien (frequency).
